summary: The _glp_detail pipeline was rewritten as a bash loop that drops CRs, skips blank lines and cuts to 200 bytes, but test/gstack-launch-probe.test.ts only feeds single-line LF output. The Windows paths this commit targets (CRLF output, leading blank or whitespace-only lines, output over 200 bytes) have no test, so a regression in the new loop would pass the suite.
fix: Add probe cases for CRLF output, leading blank and CR-only lines, and a 300-character first line, and assert the exact detail.

summary: clamp now uses bash builtins (read, pattern deletion, substring) instead of head|tr|cut, and callers dropped their own head -1 because they rely on clamp reading only the first line. Nothing tests clamp directly for multi-line input, the length cap, or the ' -~' and 'A-Za-z0-9._:/-' sets callers pass; coverage is indirect, through one hostile artifacts-sync status.
fix: Source bin/gstack-doctor's clamp in a small bash test and check first-line-only, truncation, non-ASCII bytes stripped under LC_ALL=C, and each charset callers pass.

summary: The new builtin clamp reads its line with `IFS= read -r line`. Every caller feeds it from a pipe (cso_field via sed, the browser and runtime-pins failure output via grep, the codex and floor extractions). On a pipe, bash's read cannot seek back, so it issues one read() syscall per byte and consumes the whole first line no matter how small MAX is. The old `head -1 | tr | cut` read in blocks. Measured on this machine (bash 5.2): a 300 KB single-line input takes 0.336 s (sys 0.336 s) through the new clamp against 0.019 s through the old pipeline. Syscalls cost much more under MSYS/Cygwin, so on Windows, the platform this commit optimizes for, one long unbroken first line (a minified stack trace in browser output, a long `diagnostic=` value in bin/.gstack-cso-build-result, a runaway runtime-pins line) can turn the ~60 ms saving into seconds of doctor and `--check` latency. The cost is unbounded in input size even though the output is capped at 200 characters or fewer.
fix: Bound the read to the work clamp can use, for example `IFS= read -r -n 4096 line` (or a small multiple of MAX), so each call costs a bounded number of syscalls. Add a timing-insensitive test that pipes a line over 100 KB through clamp and checks the capped output.
evidence: time (printf '%s\n' "$s" | clamp ' -~' 100), with s 300000 bytes of 'a': real 0m0.336s, sys 0m0.336s. Old pipeline: real 0m0.019s. I also checked clamp output against the old pipeline for all 8 charsets callers pass, with UTF-8, CR, control-byte and bracket inputs: identical in en_US.UTF-8 and C.UTF-8.

summary: 1. [FIXABLE] `gstack-doctor --check` now reports the wrong state-root provenance. This is a silent wrong result in the install verdict. bin/gstack-doctor:103 `cfg()` calls gstack_config_select in the doctor's own shell. gstack_config_select calls gstack_state_root_select, which overwrites the global `_gstack_sr_var`. Line ~592 already sets the shell variable `GSTACK_STATE_ROOT="$STATE_ROOT"`, so after any in-shell cfg call `_gstack_sr_var` is always "GSTACK_STATE_ROOT". In --check mode the component order is "claude codex patch codex-cli ... state-root ...". `_dc_check_codex_cli` (bin/gstack-doctor-check.sh:157) runs `cfg codex_reviews enabled` unconditionally in the current shell before `_dc_check_state_root` (lines 390/393) prints "selected by $_gstack_sr_var". Before this change, the read happened in a gstack-config subprocess and left the variable alone. Reproduced with GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/GSTACK_HOME/GSTACK_STATE_DIR/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA unset and HOME set to a scratch dir: head: PASS state-root .../h2/.gstack durable=yes (selected by GSTACK_STATE_ROOT; no GSTACK_EPHEMERAL marker; not created yet) base: PASS state-root .../h3/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default; no GSTACK_EPHEMERAL marker; not created yet) Impact: every --check verdict (the `gstack:` trailer flow that the Capy install wrapper and crews paste verbatim) claims the root came from an explicit GSTACK_STATE_ROOT. That is exactly the field docs/state-root.md says to read when diagnosing a wrong or ephemeral root, so it sends users and agents after an env var that isn't set and hides GSTACK_HOME/GSTACK_STATE_DIR/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA/default selection. The FAIL path ("is not writable ... set GSTACK_STATE_ROOT") is mislabeled the same way. No test in test/*doctor* asserts "selected by", so CI won't catch it. Non-check mode is unaffected today only because check_state_root runs before check_codex. Any reordering, or any new cfg call earlier in the run, would break it too. Fix: capture the provenance once, right after `gstack_state_root_select` at bin/gstack-doctor:~591 (for example `STATE_ROOT_VAR=$_gstack_sr_var`), and print that in check_state_root and _dc_check_state_root. Alternatively, make cfg save and restore `_gstack_sr_var` around gstack_config_select. Add a --check regression test asserting "selected by default" with the chain variables unset.

summary: 2. [INVESTIGATE, low] Launch-probe detail can now end in a partial UTF-8 sequence on macOS. bin/gstack-launch-probe.sh:36 truncates with `${line:0:200}` under LC_ALL=C (200 bytes). The old `cut -c1-200` matched this on GNU coreutils, but BSD cut on macOS counts characters in a UTF-8 locale. A binary whose first output line has multibyte text past byte ~199 (localized Windows/macOS error strings, for example) now yields a detail string with a dangling lead byte. clamp is unaffected because every clamp charset is ASCII. Only _glp_detail, which is shown raw, is exposed, and it flows into doctor rows and setup output, possibly --json. Check whether any JSON emitter or consumer (JSON.parse in bun, the install wrapper) rejects or mangles invalid UTF-8. If one does, trim back to a character boundary or route the detail through clamp ' -~'.

summary: bin/gstack-launch-probe.sh:35-36 no longer parses on bash 3.2, so gstack-doctor dies on stock macOS bash with a false "file is missing" error. The new `_glp_detail=$(set -f; IFS=...; for line in $out; do ...; case "$line" in *[![:space:]]*) ...; break ;; esac; done)` puts a case arm with no leading "(" inside a command substitution. Bash 3.2's parser closes the $( ) at the arm's ")" and fails with "syntax error near unexpected token ';;'". The file's own header (line 17) and bin/gstack-doctor:31 and bin/gstack-doctor-check.sh:12 all promise "Bash 3.2 plus POSIX tools". Evidence (bash 3.2.57): `bash -n` passes at base and fails at head for gstack-launch-probe.sh only; sourcing returns rc=1 at head and 0 at base. `bash bin/gstack-doctor --check` at head prints "gstack-doctor: /r/bin/gstack-launch-probe.sh is missing; reinstall with cd /r && ./setup" and exits 1, while base prints the full component table. Impact: bin/gstack-doctor:597 runs `. "$BIN/gstack-launch-probe.sh" 2>/dev/null || { echo "... is missing; reinstall ..."; exit 1; }`. On any Mac where `/usr/bin/env bash` resolves to /bin/bash 3.2, both plain doctor and `--check` (the install verdict that wrappers and `--for` gates read) fail hard. The stderr redirect hides the real syntax error, and the fix it suggests (reinstall) cannot help. setup:4708 (`. .../gstack-launch-probe.sh || return 0`) silently skips the probe on a bash 3.2 host as well. Fix: write the arm as `(*[![:space:]]*)` with a leading paren, or move the loop into a small function that sets _glp_detail without a command substitution. Add a bash 3.2 `bash -n` gate over bin/*.sh and the doctor files so this class of break fails CI.

summary: The new cfg() at bin/gstack-doctor:103 overwrites _gstack_sr_var, so `gstack-doctor --check` misreports where the state root came from. bin/gstack-doctor:594 sets GSTACK_STATE_ROOT="$STATE_ROOT" after the one gstack_state_root_select call. summary: clamp() at bin/gstack-doctor:98 depends on `local LC_ALL=C` changing bash's bracket-range semantics, and this is unverified on macOS /bin/bash 3.2. The old filter was tr, which matches bytes. The new one is `${line//[^$1]/}`. Bash 3.2 has no globasciiranges and resolves ranges through the locale's collation. If a function-local LC_ALL assignment does not reset the locale on 3.2, ranges such as [^a-z0-9_-] or [^ -~] can keep or strip the wrong characters in a UTF-8 locale. The clamp feeds the codex_reviews, test_backend and privacy rows and the version strings. On bash 5.2 with LANG=C.utf8 the output was correct ("é1.2.3-Ab" became "1.2.3" for '0-9.'). The bash:3.2 container has no UTF-8 locale, so I could not test 3.2. Finding 1 makes the doctor unreachable on 3.2 today, so this only matters once finding 1 is fixed. Check it on a real Mac, or use explicit character lists or POSIX classes.

summary: bin/gstack-launch-probe.sh:36 now always truncates by bytes (LC_ALL=C plus ${line:0:200}), where macOS BSD `cut -c` cut by characters in a UTF-8 locale. A localized first error line (for example a non-English Application Control message, or any UTF-8 tool output) can be split in the middle of a character. The invalid UTF-8 then flows into doctor rows and the --json output through _glp_detail (bin/gstack-doctor:344-364, doctor-check.sh:198). GNU cut on Linux and Git Bash was already byte-based, so only macOS behavior changed. Fix: trim a trailing partial UTF-8 sequence after the cut, or truncate in the caller's locale.

summary: bin/gstack-hook-check:256-260 now word-splits and pathname-expands each scanned path twice: once in `for f in $scan` and again in the unquoted `$files` passed to grep. The old `$(printf ... | awk '!seen[$0]++')` expanded it once. IFS is a newline and there is no `set -f`, so a ROOT or helper path containing *, ? or [ can expand to different files on the second pass, and the conflict-marker scan can then miss or misattribute a file. Fix: wrap the dedupe and grep in `set -f` / `set +f`, or dedupe with the old awk inside the same single expansion.
